newsitem.title: EGYPT: Strong milling stock pushes Egypt shares up.
newsitem.headline: Strong milling stock pushes Egypt shares up.

text.p: A minimum 15 percent jump in the prices of milling shares pushed Egyptian share prices towards the all-time high on Thursday.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 5.51 points to close at 253.94, 1.11 points away from the record high of 255.05, set on October 19, 1994. Turnover was an above average 36.87 million ($10.84 million).
"There was demand on all shares today. There is a lot of cash flowing into the market after last week's economic conference," said Mohammed Abdullah, vice-president of brokers EFG/Hermes.
Egypt hosted the Middle East and North Africa economic conference, attended by deleagtes from more than 90 countries.

The day's most impressive performers were the popular milling shares. Central and West Delta Flour Mills jumped 6.15 pounds to close at 75.25 after trade in shares worth more than 2.70 million pounds.
Trade worth almost two million pounds pushed Upper Egypt Flour Mills 4.80 pounds higher to 56.60 while North Cairo Flour Mills rose pounds to close at 135.25.

The cement giants continued to trade actively, with many in the sector closing at higher prices. Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA closed up 150 at 56.60 after trading in shares worth more than 2.20 million pounds.
Suez Cement saw turnover of more than 2.18 million pounds and closed at 54.00, up from 52.52. Alexandria Portland Cement closed at 64.00, down from 66.70.
The housing sector also continued to rally but Medinet Nasr Housing lost some of Wednesday's sharp gains.
The stock had Wednesday's most active on news the company was offering one free share for every share issued, switching 20 million pounds ($5.9 million) from reserves to capital.
Abdullah said the CMA put a price cap on Medinet Nasr today to prevent it from rising above 251.00 pounds. It closed on Thursday 5.25 pounds lower at 246.05.

"I don't think the price cap is a good idea because it can create a black market. It was put in place because Medinet Nasr increased by 60.00 pounds yesterday but that was a reaction to the free share," said Abdullah.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 378.98 from 370.36 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 179.38 from 175.60.
